to the acknowledgments section that send us typo corrections
and patches.

Thanks.

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] Stan v1.3 manual - typo
parts: On Mon, Jun 17, 2013 at 5:11 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

What should our process be for this?  It seems VERY
heavy to have to create a pull request to fix a single
typo, yet I don't want to pile them into other pull requests
like riders on a bill in congress.

I've been thinking about this as well.  I think it might make sense to always have a running feature branch with routine manual corrections/updates which everyone can commit to more or less free form.  This branch would then get merged either periodically, or prior to a release.

This would be distinct from changes that are meant to accompany features which I think should be in their respective feature branches.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] Stan v1.3 manual - typo
parts:
I would prefer to have pull requests. All that needs to be done is to state in one of the comments that the manual has been built and that's that.

If you can fix multiple typos at once, that's fine, but I don't care if we end up with one pull request per typo. As of now, pull requests aren't backing up due to the process taking too long. They're backing up because I missed the fact that our build was broken (misconfiguration of Jenkins and pull requests not actually being tested by the ones submitting them).

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] Stan v1.3 manual - typo
parts:
On 6/17/13 5:43 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> I would prefer to have pull requests.
OK. I'd rather have you decide because you're doing all the work!

> All that needs to be done is to state in one of the comments that the manual has
> been built and that's that.

What I was whinging on about is that I can't remember
how to do a pull request or branch, so every time I have
to pull out or doc and follow it. And I still never figured
out how to remove the merge bubbles, so I don't even know
if I'm doing the right thing with merges from develop.

Maybe you could fix our doc to indicate the right thing to do
to get rid of or work with the merge bubbles? Should I just
be pushing them? Or is there something to do to control
fast forwards? (If so, could you write it into the Wiki? I
know you explained it on e-mail, but I couldn't quite follow
the explanation then got distracted.)

> If you can fix multiple typos at once, that's fine, but I don't care if we end up with one pull request per typo. As of
> now, pull requests aren't backing up due to the process taking too long. They're backing up because I missed the fact
> that our build was broken (misconfiguration of Jenkins and pull requests not actually being tested by the ones
> submitting them).

I'm just finding all the traffic about testing and
what-not very hard to follow, so I just ignore most of it.
As such, it adds noise to the signal I'm getting about the
state of our system, the sum total of which is that I'm
pretty confused about where we're at. I'm sure I'll eventually
get the hang of it so it doesn't feel so clunky.

- Bob
